title: The books
hookLine: the Torah of Musa, the Psalms of Dawud, the Gospel of Isa, the Scrolls of Ibrahim, and the Qur'an

cards: Here's an unusual article of faith: it asks Muslims to believe in books that may never sit on their own shelves. The third of the six is the books, kutub in Arabic.
Not only the Qur'an at home, perhaps wrapped in cloth on a high shelf. Also a scroll given to Ibrahim. A law given to Musa.
Songs given to Dawud. A gospel given to Isa, the name the Qur'an uses for Jesus. Five books, five messengers, one belief that holds them together.

teach.b: First, the names. The Qur'an names the Tawrat, the Torah, given to Musa, Moses. The Zabur, the Psalms, given to Dawud, David; in Pickthall's words, "We imparted unto David the Psalms."
The Injil, the Gospel, given to Isa. And at the end of a short surah, a fourth: "Lo! This is in the former scrolls, The Books of Abraham and Moses." With the Qur'an itself, that makes five.
The Qur'an speaks of itself as confirming what was revealed before it, the Torah and the Gospel among them.
In Muslim teaching the message across the books is the same at its heart: worship the One, do good, a day of reckoning is coming. Third, what the belief is and isn't.

It's belief in those books as they were revealed to their messengers. The Qur'an is held to be the last book and the measure of the others, and Muslim scholars discuss how the earlier texts reached us.
Jews and Christians read their own scriptures on their own terms; this path just says who holds what. Last, a phrase.
In one verse the Arabic reads, word by word, for every term, a book. Pickthall renders it, "For everything there is a time prescribed."
Some readers hear in it the same idea as this article of faith: no age was left without a word from its Lord.

how: Muslims affirm belief in the revealed books, naming the Tawrat, Zabur, Injil, the scrolls of Ibrahim and the Qur'an, and a Qur'an at home may be kept on a high shelf, sometimes wrapped in cloth.

games.q: how does the Qur'an describe its relation to the earlier books?
o: it confirms what was revealed before it.
it says they were never revealed.
games.why: the Qur'an calls itself confirming what came before, naming the Torah and the Gospel, and Muslims treat it as the last book.

practice: Picture a single shelf and set five books on it one by one, saying each name as you place it: the scrolls of Ibrahim, the Torah of Musa, the Psalms of Dawud, the Gospel of Isa, the Qur'an, brought to the Prophet Muhammad ﷺ.
Then look at the whole shelf for a while. If you pray, you can ask to understand what your own book asks of you; if not, just rest your eyes on the shelf.

wordCard.voice: Kutub. Books; the plural of kitab. The third article of faith: belief in the books Allah revealed to His messengers. Today's word.

orig.note: Arabic: books; the singular is kitab, كتاب.
